about: Think Tank Showdown question pools per level. Each round has a pool (qs); every new game draws "play" main questions and "spares" spare questions at random from it. kind: answer / ideas / wager. todo = something for Henry to check. The first questions of each M.3 round are the original set; the rest were written for Kru.

rounds.name: Riddle Rush
rounds.rule: 45 seconds. Write ONE answer. Hold it up on "Show me!" · 1 point

qs.q: What has a face and two hands, but no arms or legs?
qs.why: A clock has a face and two hands: the hour hand and the minute hand.

qs.q: What has to be broken before you can use it?
qs.why: You break an egg before you cook it.

qs.q: What goes up but never comes down?
qs.why: Every birthday your age goes up. It never goes down!

qs.q: I have lots of teeth, but I can't bite. What am I?
qs.why: Also accept: a zip / a saw.

qs.q: What has legs but can't walk?
qs.why: Also accept: a chair / a bed.

qs.q: What is full of holes but can still hold water?
What can you hear but not see or touch? You use it when you speak.
qs.why: Also accept: a sound.

qs.q: What gets bigger the more you take away from it?
qs.why: Dig more and the hole gets bigger!

qs.q: What goes up when the rain comes down?
qs.why: You open it when it rains.

qs.q: What has one head, one foot and four legs?
qs.why: The head and foot of the bed, and four legs.

qs.q: I am yellow and I shine in the day. What am I?
What has a mouth but never eats, and a bed but never sleeps?
qs.why: The mouth and bed of a river.

qs.q: What can you break without touching it?
What has lots of words but never speaks?
qs.why: Also accept: a dictionary / a newspaper.

qs.q: What has a ring but no finger?
qs.why: The phone rings!

qs.q: I have cities but no houses, and rivers but no water. What am I?
What has a head and a tail but no body?
qs.why: Heads or tails?

qs.q: What is white when it is dirty and black when it is clean?
qs.why: Chalk makes it white.

qs.q: What can fill a room but takes up no space?
qs.why: Also accept: air / sound.

qs.q: What starts with T, ends with T, and has T in it?
qs.why: Tea in a T-pot!

rounds.name: Spot the Problem
rounds.rule: 60 s to talk in your team. Hands up to answer. A NEW speaker each time · Right = 2 · Steal = 1

qs.q: "My cat is black. So all cats are black."
qs.a: One cat can't tell you about all cats.
qs.why: Award 2 for: only one cat / you can't say "all" / there are white, orange and gray cats.

qs.q: "I ate an ice cream and then it rained. So ice cream makes it rain."
qs.a: The two things happened together, but one didn't cause the other.
qs.why: Award 2 for: it was just at the same time / ice cream can't change the weather.

qs.q: "This phone is the best because it is the most expensive."
qs.a: Expensive doesn't always mean the best.
qs.why: Award 2 for: price isn't quality / you need to check what the phone can do.

qs.q: "Everyone in my class has a phone. So every child in the world has a phone."
qs.a: One class is too small to say something about the whole world.
qs.why: Award 2 for: small group / some children are poor / you can't say "every".

qs.q: "My brother is tall, so he must be good at basketball."
qs.a: Being tall doesn't make you good at a sport.
qs.why: Award 2 for: you need practice / skill, not just height.

qs.q: "I saw one rude tourist. So all tourists are rude."
qs.a: One person can't tell you about everyone.
qs.why: Award 2 for: only one person / you can't say "all".

qs.q: "My team lost today. So my team is the worst team in the world."
qs.why: Award 2 for: only one game / they can win next time.

qs.q: "Everybody has a new phone, so you need one too."
qs.a: Doing what everyone does isn't a good reason.
qs.why: Award 2 for: do you really need it? / you can decide for yourself.

qs.q: "If you don't like dogs, you must love cats."
qs.a: There are more than two choices.
qs.why: Award 2 for: you can like neither / you can like both.

qs.q: "I didn't study and I passed. So studying is not important."
qs.a: One lucky time doesn't prove it.
qs.why: Award 2 for: you were lucky / most people need to study.

qs.q: "This store is near my house, so it is the best store."
qs.why: Award 2 for: other stores can be better or cheaper.

qs.q: "My friend is good at math, so she is good at English too."
qs.a: Good at one thing doesn't mean good at everything.
qs.why: Award 2 for: they are different subjects.

qs.q: "It's on the internet, so it must be true."
qs.why: Award 2 for: anyone can write online / check other places.

qs.q: "The new student is quiet, so she must be unfriendly."
qs.why: Award 2 for: she may be shy / she is new.

rounds.name: What Would Happen If…?
rounds.rule: 90 s: write as many results as you can. Then each team says one NEW idea · 1 point each, 2 times round

qs.q: What would happen if it rained every day for a month?
qs.why: Floods · no outdoor sport · wet clothes · plants grow fast · people stay at home · stores sell lots of umbrellas.

qs.q: What would happen if there were no cars?
qs.why: People walk or ride bikes · cleaner air · trips take longer · quieter streets · more buses and trains.

qs.q: What would happen if animals could talk?
qs.why: Pets tell us what they want · zoos change · farmers talk to their animals · new job: animal translator.

qs.q: What would happen if there was no school for a year?
qs.why: More free time · students forget what they learned · parents need childcare · more online lessons · friends miss each other.

qs.q: What would happen if everyone had a pet dinosaur?
qs.why: Big houses and gardens · lots of food needed · dinosaur parks · traffic problems · dinosaur doctors.

qs.q: What would happen if it was always night?
qs.why: No sun for plants · cold weather · lights on all day · people sleep more · stars all the time.

qs.q: What would happen if people could fly?
qs.why: No need for cars · fewer traffic jams · new sky rules · more accidents? · birds are surprised!

qs.q: What would happen if there was no ice cream?
qs.why: Sad children · ice cream shops close · people eat other candy · less sugar · new desserts.

rounds.name: Final Wager
rounds.rule: BEFORE you see it: write your bet (0–5 points). Right = win your bet · Wrong = lose it

qs.q: A farmer has 5 cows. All but 2 run away. How many cows are left?
qs.why: "All but 2" means "all of them except 2". So 2 cows stay.
qs.todo: "All but 2" may be new English for M.1: explain it after the answer.

qs.q: Which month has 28 days?
qs.why: Every month has at least 28 days!

qs.q: How many legs do 3 chickens have?
qs.why: A chicken has 2 legs: 3 × 2 = 6.

qs.q: Take half of 10, then add 2. What is the answer?
qs.why: Half of 10 is 5. 5 + 2 = 7.

qs.q: Today is Monday. What day will it be in 3 days?
qs.why: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday.

qs.q: A dog is bigger than a cat. A cat is bigger than a mouse. Which is the smallest?
How many months have 31 days?
qs.why: January, March, May, July, August, October and December.

qs.q: I have 2 coins. Together they make 15 baht. One of them is not a 5-baht coin. What are they?
qs.why: One is not a 5-baht coin (it is the 10). The other one is!

rounds.name: Riddle Rush
rounds.rule: 40 seconds. Write ONE answer. Hold it up on "Show me!" · 1 point

qs.q: What can travel around the world while staying in a corner?
qs.why: A stamp stays in the corner of an envelope while the letter travels.

qs.q: What has a neck but no head?
qs.why: Also accept: a shirt / a guitar.

qs.q: What belongs to you, but other people use it more than you do?
qs.why: Other people say your name much more often than you do.

qs.q: I'm tall when I'm young and short when I'm old. What am I?
qs.why: A candle gets shorter as it burns.

qs.q: What has one eye but can't see?
qs.why: The thread goes through the needle's eye.

qs.q: What can you hold in your right hand but never in your left hand?
qs.why: Also accept: your left elbow.

qs.q: What comes down but never goes up?
qs.why: Also accept: snow.

qs.q: I have keys but no locks, and space but no room. What am I?
qs.why: The space bar!

qs.q: What has a thumb and four fingers but is not alive?
What goes through cities and fields but never moves?
qs.why: Also accept: a railway / a path.

qs.q: What can't talk but answers when you speak to it?
What has a bottom at the top?
qs.why: Your bottom is at the top of your legs!

qs.q: What invention lets you look right through a wall?
If you drop me, I crack. If you smile at me, I smile back. What am I?
What kind of room has no doors or windows?
qs.why: Mush-ROOM.

qs.q: What is so fragile that saying its name breaks it?
What has 13 hearts but no other body parts?
qs.why: 13 cards are hearts.

qs.q: Which word is spelled wrong in every dictionary?
qs.why: W-R-O-N-G!

qs.q: What goes up and down but doesn't move?
qs.why: Also accept: a staircase.

qs.q: I am an odd number. Take away one letter and I become even. What number am I?
qs.why: S-even.

rounds.name: Spot the Problem
rounds.rule: 45 s to discuss. Hands up to answer. A NEW speaker each time · Right = 2 · Steal = 1

qs.q: "My grandfather smoked all his life and lived to 95. So smoking isn't bad for you."
qs.a: One person's story doesn't prove something for everyone.
qs.why: Award 2 for: only one example / he was lucky / doctors study many people, not one.

qs.q: "9 out of 10 movie stars use this shampoo. It will make your hair beautiful."
qs.a: The stars may be paid, and their hair is beautiful for other reasons.
qs.why: Award 2 for: it's an advert / who asked the stars? / no proof the shampoo did it.

qs.q: "If we let students use phones at break, soon they will use them in every lesson, and then nobody will learn anything."
qs.a: One small change doesn't have to lead to the worst result.
qs.why: Award 2 for: that's a big jump / rules can stop it / it might not happen.

qs.q: "Lots of people believe it, so it must be true."
qs.a: Many people can still be wrong.
qs.why: Award 2 for: popular isn't the same as true / check the facts.

qs.q: "You don't play soccer, so your ideas about the team are wrong."
qs.a: Judge the idea, not the person.
qs.why: Award 2 for: anyone can have a good idea / look at the reasons.

qs.q: "Ten people liked this restaurant online, so it must be the best in Thailand."
qs.a: Ten reviews are too few to say "the best in Thailand".
qs.why: Award 2 for: small number / maybe they are friends / other restaurants.

qs.q: "Don't listen to her advice about food. She's only 14."
qs.a: Age doesn't make an idea right or wrong.
qs.why: Award 2 for: listen to the idea, not the age.

qs.q: "If you eat one sweet, you'll eat the whole bag, and then all your teeth will fall out!"
qs.a: One small thing won't always lead to the worst result.
qs.why: Award 2 for: that's a big jump / you can stop at one.

qs.q: "Either you come to my party or you're not my friend."
qs.a: There are more than two choices.
qs.why: Award 2 for: you can be a friend and still miss a party.

qs.q: "Most of my class says the test was easy, so it was easy for everyone."
qs.why: Award 2 for: other people may find it hard.

qs.q: "This medicine is natural, so it can't be bad for you."
qs.why: Award 2 for: some plants are poisonous / ask a doctor.

qs.q: "I've never seen a crocodile in this river, so there are no crocodiles here."
qs.a: Not seeing something doesn't prove it isn't there.
qs.why: Award 2 for: they can hide / you need more proof.

qs.q: "The price went up, so the quality must be better."
qs.a: A higher price doesn't prove better quality.
qs.why: Award 2 for: maybe they just want more money.

qs.q: "Our team always wins on Fridays, so we will win this Friday."
qs.a: The past doesn't guarantee the future.
qs.why: Award 2 for: the other team may be better / it was luck.

rounds.name: What Would Happen If…?
rounds.rule: 90 s: list as many results as you can. Then each team says one NEW idea · 1 point each, 2 times round

qs.q: What would happen if homework was banned in every school?
qs.why: More free time · more sleep · some students forget lessons · more time for family, sport or part-time jobs · teachers change how they teach.

qs.q: What would happen if everyone in Thailand could speak only English for one day?
qs.why: Stores and taxis have problems · people use their hands to explain · lots of laughing · English improves fast · the TV news changes.

qs.q: What would happen if people could live for 200 years?
qs.why: More people on Earth · people work for longer · families with six generations · we need more food and houses.

qs.q: What would happen if there was no electricity for a week?
qs.why: No phones or internet · food goes bad · candles and flashlights · no air conditioning · people talk more.

qs.q: What would happen if everyone in the world spoke the same language?
qs.why: Easy travel · no English lessons! · more friends abroad · some cultures change · no translators needed.

qs.q: What would happen if tourists stopped coming to Thailand?
qs.why: Hotels close · people lose jobs · quieter beaches · less money · new kinds of business.

qs.q: What would happen if you could be invisible for one day?
qs.why: Play tricks · hear secrets · go anywhere free · nobody sees you in photos · people get scared.

qs.q: What would happen if school was only online?
qs.why: No travel to school · more screen time · less sport · miss friends · learn at home.

rounds.name: Final Wager
rounds.rule: BEFORE you see it: write your bet (0–5 points). Right = win your bet · Wrong = lose it

qs.q: You are running a race and you pass the person in second place. What place are you in now?
qs.why: You took their place. The person you passed is now third.

qs.q: A bat and a ball cost 110 baht together. The bat costs 100 baht more than the ball. How much is the ball?
qs.why: Ball 5 + bat 105 = 110. (Not 10 baht: then the bat is 110 and the total is 120.)

qs.q: There are 3 apples. You take away 2. How many apples do YOU have?
qs.why: You took 2, so you have 2!

qs.q: Which is heavier: a kilo of feathers or a kilo of stones?
qs.a: Neither: they both weigh a kilo.

qs.q: A doctor gives you 3 pills. Take one every 30 minutes. How many minutes until they are all gone?
qs.why: One now, one at 30 minutes, one at 60 minutes.

qs.q: How many times do you write the number 1 when you count from 1 to 20?
What is the next number? 2, 4, 8, 16, …
qs.why: Each number doubles.

qs.q: Which is correct: "The yolk of the egg is white" or "The yolk of the egg are white"?

rounds.name: Riddle Rush
rounds.rule: 40 seconds. Write ONE answer. Hold it up on "Show me!" · 1 point

qs.q: What has keys but can't open locks?
qs.why: Also accept: a keyboard / a computer keyboard.

qs.q: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?
qs.why: Every step you take leaves a footprint behind you.

qs.q: What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years?
qs.why: Look at the spelling: minute, moMent, thousand years.

qs.q: Before Mount Everest was discovered, what was the highest mountain in the world?
qs.why: It was still the highest. People just didn't know yet!

qs.q: What can you catch but not throw?
qs.why: Also accept: a cough / the flu.

qs.q: What gets wetter the more it dries?
What is always coming but never arrives?
qs.why: When it arrives, it is today.

qs.q: What can be cracked, made, told and played?
What begins with E, ends with E, but usually has only one letter in it?
qs.why: One letter inside it!

qs.q: What word becomes shorter when you add two letters to it?
qs.why: Short + er = shorter.

qs.q: Forwards I am heavy, but backwards I am not. What am I?
qs.why: Ton backwards is "not".

qs.q: What can you hold without touching it?
qs.why: Also accept: a conversation.

qs.q: If you have me, you want to share me. If you share me, you haven't got me. What am I?
A man walked in the rain with no umbrella or hat, but not one hair on his head got wet. Why?
What can you see once in a year, twice in a week, but never in a day?
qs.why: Look at the spelling: yEar, wEEk, day.

qs.q: What has to be answered but never asks a question?
qs.why: Also accept: a doorbell.

qs.q: I have branches but no fruit, trunk or leaves. What am I?
qs.why: Banks have branches in many towns.

qs.q: Which room do ghosts never go into?
qs.why: Ghosts aren't living!

qs.q: Two fathers and two sons go fishing. They catch three fish and each gets one. How?
qs.a: There are only 3 people: a grandfather, a father and a son.

qs.q: What four-letter word reads the same forwards, backwards and upside down?

rounds.name: Spot the Problem
rounds.rule: 45 s to discuss. Hands up to answer. A NEW speaker each time · Right = 2 · Steal = 1

qs.q: "I wore my red socks and passed my math test. So red socks help you pass tests."
qs.a: Two things happened together, but one didn't cause the other.
qs.why: Award 2 for: coincidence / no proof the socks did it / she passed because she studied.

qs.q: "All five of my friends love K-pop. So every teenager in Thailand loves K-pop."
qs.a: Five people are too few to say something about everyone.
qs.why: Award 2 for: small group / you can't generalise / your friends are similar to you.

qs.q: "A famous soccer player drinks this energy drink. So it must make you run faster."
qs.a: The soccer player is paid to say it. He was fast before the drink.
qs.why: Award 2 for: advertising / he's paid / no evidence about the drink itself.

qs.q: "Nobody has proved that ghosts are NOT real. So ghosts must be real."
qs.a: No proof against something isn't proof for it.
qs.why: Award 2 for: the person saying 'ghosts are real' needs the evidence.

qs.q: "You either love this school or you hate it."
qs.a: There are more than two choices.
qs.why: Award 2 for: you can like some parts and not others / it's in the middle.

qs.q: "Crime went up after the new mall opened. So the mall caused the crime."
qs.a: Two things happening together doesn't prove one caused the other.
qs.why: Award 2 for: other reasons / more people in the area / need evidence.

qs.q: "Everyone is buying this new coin, so it's a smart investment."
qs.why: Award 2 for: following the crowd / prices can fall.

qs.q: "We've always done it this way, so it's the right way."
qs.a: Tradition alone isn't a good reason.
qs.why: Award 2 for: there may be a better way now.

qs.q: "You either support every new school rule or you don't care about safety."
qs.a: There are more than two positions.
qs.why: Award 2 for: you can agree with some rules and not others.

qs.q: "He's a great soccer player, so his advice about medicine must be right."
qs.a: Being an expert in one thing doesn't make you an expert in another.
qs.why: Award 2 for: ask a doctor / wrong kind of expert.

qs.q: "If we ban junk food at school, next they'll ban all the food we like."
qs.a: One rule doesn't have to lead to an extreme result.
qs.why: Award 2 for: slippery slope / that's a big jump.

qs.q: "Nobody complained about the new schedule, so everyone loves it."
qs.a: Silence isn't the same as agreement.
qs.why: Award 2 for: maybe they didn't dare / didn't know how to complain.

qs.q: "That scientist was wrong once, so all her research is wrong."
qs.a: One mistake doesn't make everything wrong.
qs.why: Award 2 for: judge each piece of research on its evidence.

qs.q: "This app has a million downloads, so it must be safe."
qs.a: Popular isn't the same as safe.
qs.why: Award 2 for: check privacy / reviews / who made it.

rounds.name: What Would Happen If…?
rounds.rule: 90 s: list as many results as you can. Then each team says one NEW idea · 1 point each, 2 times round

qs.q: What would happen if school started at 11 a.m.?
qs.why: Students sleep more · school finishes later · more traffic in the evening · parents need childcare in the morning · less time for homework or sport.

qs.q: What would happen if nobody could tell a lie for one whole day?
qs.why: Friendships break · honest reviews · surprise parties fail · politicians in trouble · fewer arguments later?

qs.q: What would happen if every phone stopped working for one week?
qs.why: People talk face to face · get lost (no maps) · banks and stores have problems · less screen time · emergencies are harder.

qs.q: What would happen if robots did all the jobs?
qs.why: People lose jobs · more free time · need new skills · cheaper products · who earns money?

qs.q: What would happen if the internet disappeared forever?
qs.why: Letters and phone calls · libraries busy again · banks and stores have problems · less fake news · businesses close.

qs.q: What would happen if everyone lived to 150?
qs.why: More people on Earth · work for longer · huge families · need more food and homes · new hobbies.

qs.q: What would happen if money didn't exist?
qs.why: Swap things (barter) · harder to save · no banks · people share more? · prices disappear.

qs.q: What would happen if Thailand had snow every winter?
qs.why: Ski resorts · warm clothes in stores · tourists come for snow · crops change · snow days off school.

rounds.name: Final Wager
rounds.rule: BEFORE you see it: write your bet (0–5 points). Right = win your bet · Wrong = lose it

qs.q: A girl has as many brothers as sisters. Each brother has only half as many brothers as sisters. How many brothers and sisters are in the family?
qs.why: The girl sees 3 other sisters and 3 brothers. A brother sees 2 brothers and 4 sisters (2 is half of 4).

qs.q: How many times can you take 10 away from 100?
qs.why: After that, you are taking 10 away from 90!

qs.q: 5 machines make 5 phones in 5 minutes. How long do 100 machines take to make 100 phones?
qs.why: Each machine makes one phone in 5 minutes.

qs.q: A water plant doubles in size every day. It covers a lake in 30 days. On which day did it cover half the lake?
qs.why: It doubles from half to full on the last day.

qs.q: What is the next number? 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …
qs.why: Add the two numbers before: 5 + 8 = 13.

qs.q: You are in a race and you pass the person in LAST place. What place are you in now?
qs.a: It's impossible: nobody is behind the last person.

qs.q: A father has five daughters. Each daughter has one brother. How many children are there?
qs.why: Five daughters and ONE brother (they share him).

qs.q: You write all the numbers from 1 to 100. How many times do you write the number 9?
